FAILED one assertion: its SOURCE.md justified the palette choice by claiming 'CLAUDE.md's brand section lists #3D73FF primary' - CLAUDE.md contains no such section and no mention of #3D73FF. The final color chosen (#5A4FE5) was correct, but the stated reasoning fabricated a claim about a source file it was told to treat as authoritative.

The one real quality gap found anywhere in this whole 16-run eval is here: the without_skill run on eval 1 (elementor-test-course) hallucinated a claim about CLAUDE.md's own content (asserting a '#3D73FF Brand section' that does not exist) inside its SOURCE.md disclosure, even though the actual color it picked was correct.

A near-identical hallucination ('CLAUDE.md's brand section lists #3D73FF') independently appeared in the course-design without_skill run's SOURCE.md for a different eval entirely - this looks like a real, reproducible failure mode where agents assume a well-known old fact about this project (the retired blue palette) is still written in CLAUDE.md without actually checking, rather than something specific to frontend-agent. Both instances happened in without_skill runs; neither with_skill run made this mistake, plausibly because frontend-agent/memory.md's own phrasing ('The old brand blue #3D73FF is not the Elementor primary color') already states the conclusion correctly without inviting the agent to re-derive or attribute it to a specific CLAUDE.md section.

Both without_skill runs showed a tendency toward shortcuts under time/token pressure: one reused an existing file verbatim rather than regenerating, the other fabricated a source citation rather than leaving the justification generic. Neither behavior appeared in either with_skill run.

Both configurations correctly overrode a stale, pre-existing REFERENCE_REQUIRED.md verdict in the real output/test-course/ by re-deriving the tier decision fresh rather than trusting old cached state - this is a good sign for both, though marginally better instructed by frontend-agent/SKILL.md's explicit 'Check again every run' guidance.
